claim_register.text: sleep-health-hackathon-v0 evaluates seven sleep-health prediction targets (Q1, Q2, Q3, S1, S2, S3, S4) on sleep-lifelog-2024 under a locally locked GroupKFold-by-subject-id sprint-1 policy with 3 folds, and reports a grouped macro log-loss aggregated as a macro mean across targets.

Allowed claim boundaries against this benchmark are local_oof_diagnostic_only, same_split_baseline_comparison, and public_lb_observation_only. Public leaderboard scores require a DACON submission and are reported separately from local OOF diagnostic scores.

An unseen-subject generalization track (Track A) is the recommended main track; a same-subject temporal forecasting track (Track B) is recorded as a separate candidate and must not be conflated with Track A, especially for Q-family targets that are participant-relative averages.

sleep-lifelog-2024 is a multimodal smartphone, smartwatch, sleep-sensor, and self-report dataset of about 700 days recorded in 2024 with seven prediction targets (Q1, Q2, Q3, S1, S2, S3, S4). The released training labels are in ch2026_metrics_train.csv and produce a 450-row modeling table grouped by subject_id.

The local canonical evaluation split for sprint 1 is GroupKFold by subject_id with 3 folds on the released training labels. Some older docs framed only six targets; the released package takes precedence over those older notes.
Q-family labels are participant-relative averages and therefore at very high leakage risk under same-subject splits; objective S-family labels reflect guideline compliance.

open_questions: Has an organizer-official validation or split protocol been published after the local sprint-1 GroupKFold policy was recorded?
Where is the durable fold assignment artifact for the canonical 3-fold GroupKFold split, and should it be versioned separately from the decision page?
Are the sleep-sensor and self-report schemas fully available beyond the placeholder and bedtime-questionnaire references in the packet?
What exact aggregation recipes should be used for nested modality payloads and minute-level streams before tabular modeling?
Which historical notes or paper summaries contain the six-target framing, and should they be annotated as superseded by the released package and metric description?
Do future experiment packets report Q-family and S-family metrics separately in addition to grouped macro log-loss?
Which DACON submission ids, if any, correspond to public leaderboard observations, and are private leaderboard results available?
How should Track B same-subject temporal forecasting be evaluated without being confused with Track A unseen-subject generalization?
review_notes: All raw packet claims keep `tentative` status. No claim was promoted to supported.
No metric values, model rankings, leaderboard scores, or performance comparisons are introduced.
The synthesis is review-required because it interprets leakage risk, evaluation boundaries, and cross-page wiki structure.
The allowed output surface is limited to the ten requested wiki pages; no raw, automation, or policy file is written.
Entity pages now emphasize stable dataset and benchmark memory, while packet ids and raw provenance are preserved in provenance sections.
superseded_or_conflicting_claims: The packets record a six-target older-summary framing as superseded by the released package and metric description that include seven targets, including S4. This supersession remains packet-level tentative evidence until reviewed against the raw released package.
Track A unseen-subject generalization and Track B same-subject temporal forecasting answer different questions and must not be merged into one benchmark claim.
Public leaderboard observations on the DACON public split are noisy directional observations and do not supersede local OOF diagnostic claims or private leaderboard outcomes.
The local canonical GroupKFold-by-subject split is not an organizer-official split protocol; an organizer-published protocol would supersede or amend the current decision page.
synthesis_summary: Integrated the 2026-05-29 Sleep Lifelog dataset and Sleep Health Hackathon benchmark packets into stable wiki memory. The pass rewrites both entity pages, creates cross-cutting feature, evaluation-decision, open-question, and synthesis-report pages, and updates overview, latest context, index, and log. All source claims remain tentative; no performance, leaderboard, or model-quality claim is promoted.
